text: CHAPTER 5: RESULT ANALYSIS

This chapter reports the results obtained from the portion of the system implemented to date. The sidecar entry point, the six-factor scoring engine, the full pattern catalog, the vault, the lineage tracker and their supporting scripts are implemented and functional. The multi-stage pipeline restructuring, the SecretBench pattern import, the ML weight-training run on the 50,000-line corpus, the Aho–Corasick prefilter, the active validity Analyzer, the mutating admission webhook and the observability layer are planned for the phased work described in Chapter 3. Section 5.6 states the completion status explicitly.

text: 2. DATASET AND MODULE INVENTORY

The current benchmark dataset consists of a file of 1,847 log lines together with a line-labelled ground-truth file used to compute precision, recall and related metrics. The pattern catalog underlying the classifier comprises more than 600 hand-crafted patterns spanning cloud providers, AI-service keys, databases, messaging services, payment providers, version-control and CI/CD tokens, private keys and generic high-entropy fallbacks, together with 761 SecretBench-validated patterns planned for integration in Phase 0.

3. COMPARATIVE MODEL PERFORMANCE
The system was evaluated on the 1,847-line labelled dataset. Table 5.3 reports the resulting precision, recall, F1-score, throughput and latency figures.

Figure 5.2: Per-line latency: average, P95 and P99 against the 5 ms design target

All three latency percentiles are well below the 5 ms design target (NFR1) and the throughput of 12,847 lines/sec exceeds the 5,000 lines/sec minimum (NFR2). The current benchmark is on 1,847 lines; the four-way ablation experiment on a 50,000-line corpus is planned for Phase 2 and its expected results are discussed in Chapter 6.

The four-way ablation experiment described in Chapter 3 compares a regex-only baseline, a regex-plus-entropy baseline, the current six-factor SCS model and the full multi-stage pipeline with SecretBench patterns. Its expected F1 values are 0.71, 0.77, 0.89 and 0.98 respectively. These figures have not yet been measured; the experiment awaits the 50,000-line corpus (Phase 2). They are shown as a hypothesis chart in Figure 6.1 in Chapter 6.
4. DETECTION QUALITY AND FAILURE MODES
The false-positive cases observed on the current benchmark were analysed by root cause. Table 5.4 reports the five most frequent patterns and the planned fix for each.
Table 5.4: False-positive analysis: top five patterns

data: Entropy near threshold; no negative keyword suppression
Decodes to JSON, not a secret

text: Figure 5.3: Top five false-positive patterns (left) and total error count (right) on the 1,847-line dataset

The 31 false negatives were analysed and fall into three root causes: secrets at the very start of a line where the key-value regex does not fire (covered by Pass 2 of the Secret Classifier, edge case EC-08, which is already handled); URL-encoded secrets that are not decoded before scoring (edge case EC-05, fix planned in Phase 3); and multi-line PEM keys whose body lines score below the threshold when evaluated independently (edge case EC-01, multi-line buffering planned in Phase 3).
